sources.entry: Etherpad - Highly customizable online editor providing collaborative editing in real-time. (Demo, Source Code) Apache-2.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: Etherpad is a self-hostable real-time collaborative document editor that attributes every edit to its author and keeps full revision history.
summary.what_it_does: Etherpad lets multiple people edit the same document simultaneously in a browser, with each keystroke attributed to its author and colour-coded author marks shown in the text. A timeslider lets users scrub through the full revision history of a pad. The README says it runs on your own server, offers a built-in full data export, and has an HTTP API (with OpenAPI definitions at /api/openapi.json) for managing pads, users and groups. Functionality is extended through a plugin framework, with plugins installable from the admin web interface or the command line. The README also mentions a jQuery plugin for embedding pads in websites and translations into many languages via TranslateWiki.
use_cases: tracking authorship and edit history of a document
embedding collaborative pads in a website
running a team or classroom shared editor
public consultation or drafting with many editors
how_to_run: git clone -b master the Etherpad repository
pnpm run prod, then open Etherpad in a browser
notable: Per-keystroke author attribution with colour-coded authorship and a timeslider for full revision history
Plugin framework with many plugins; suggested plugin set includes markdown, comments, and WebRTC
Documented HTTP API with OpenAPI definitions
Official Docker image on both Docker Hub and GitHub Container Registry
caveats: README recommends a dedicated database such as mysql or postgres for production, since the dirtyDB driver is only for testing and development
README says the project is maintained by a small volunteer team and is actively looking for maintainers
Two opt-out network calls are made by Etherpad's own code, documented in PRIVACY.md
keywords: work on a document together live
track who changed what in a document
host my own shared writing pad
open source etherpad alternative to hosted docs
